briefings.title: Personalized Weekly Briefing — October 23, 2026
briefings.theme: The proactive-agent race just became practical.
briefings.deck: Claude Duet brings an approval-first agent to connected cloud apps; ChatGPT can now build collaborative slide decks; Gemini is turning messy financial inputs into interactive models; and xAI published a concrete pattern for event-driven monitoring. The final card tracks the week’s sharp energy-and-rates signal.

stories.headline: Claude Duet pairs proactive work with explicit approvals
stories.summary: Claude Duet is a separate proactive-agent app that checks connected accounts, searches prior Claude chats, brings back sourced summaries, and pauses before sending email, paying, signing, or deleting. It is available only through a U.S. waitlist for Pro and Max users, with access opening in waves.
stories.whatChanged: Restrictions: U.S.-only waitlist, Pro or Max, invitation required; Team and Enterprise are not yet supported. It runs on Opus 5.5, uses normal plan limits—including background checks—and cannot be watched or taken over in its browser. Microsoft 365 is not yet available and Slack is limited.
stories.whyItMatters: This is close to the approval-first cloud pattern you want for property-tour intake and inbox cleanup: collect evidence automatically, but hold consequential actions for review.
stories.prompt: Create a read-only morning check across my connected Gmail and Drive. Report: new property-tour emails, listing-status changes, missing source files, and anything requiring my decision. Cite the exact email or file for every item. Do not send, delete, move, purchase, sign, or change anything. Group proposed actions into one approval list.

links.label: Anthropic · Get started with Claude Duet

stories.headline: ChatGPT Slides turns source files into a shared, editable deck
stories.summary: ChatGPT Slides can start from a conversation, uploaded files, an outline, or an example deck, then let collaborators edit text, shapes, images, and charts in real time. On the web it exports to PowerPoint, PDF, or Google Slides, which makes it practical for manager-ready audit status and issue presentations.
stories.whatChanged: Access: rolling out to eligible Pro, Business, and Enterprise users with Space access on web and desktop. Web export supports PowerPoint, PDF, and Google Slides. Managed-workspace availability depends on admin settings.
stories.whyItMatters: Your numbered SEFA issues, TB/GL bridges, and manager emails can now feed one living deck instead of being reformatted separately for each review meeting.
stories.prompt: Create a concise manager-review deck from the attached SEFA issues workbook and supporting memo. Use: executive status; issue-by-issue bridge; amounts and evidence citations; decisions needed; and next actions. Keep observed facts separate from conclusions. Add speaker notes with the exact source file and cell or section for every amount. Export to PowerPoint only after I approve the outline.

stories.headline: Gemini’s new business hub turns messy finance inputs into interactive models
stories.summary: Google is adding a central small-business workspace in Gemini that connects Google Workspace plus services such as Dropbox, Shopify, Xero, Canva, Wix, and Zoho. Its finance workflow is designed to transform spreadsheets, receipts, and purchase records into graphics and interactive models in seconds.
stories.whatChanged: Availability: Google says the tools are rolling out globally over the coming days; plan-by-plan access was not specified in the announcement. Connected-app availability can differ by account and region. Use only firm-approved client data.
stories.whyItMatters: The workflow matches your recurring need to turn TBs, GLs, receipts, and property-budget exports into an understandable decision view without hand-building every chart.
stories.prompt: Using this approved trial balance and account map, create an interactive financial model with fund, department, natural account, and period filters. Tie every visual to a reconciliation table. Show unmapped accounts, duplicate mappings, missing periods, and totals that do not agree. Do not change the source workbook or treat classifications as audited conclusions.

links.label: Google · New Gemini tools for small business owners

stories.headline: Grok Bot shows a concrete event-monitoring pattern: detect, hold, approve, sweep
stories.summary: xAI described two cloud teammates: one checks the preceding 15 minutes of support tickets every five minutes for spikes, while another prepares an approved batch once an incident is resolved. In one example, a human-reviewed sweep cleared 204 related tickets in about 10 minutes.
stories.whatChanged: This is a newly published implementation pattern, not a new entitlement. Grok Bot access still depends on your subscription or enterprise setup. The useful design is the separation between detection, temporary holding, a human-reviewed batch, and final action.
stories.whyItMatters: The same pattern can protect your property-brief ingestion and PBC workflows from duplicate emails, clustered failures, or partial updates while keeping one approval gate.
stories.prompt: Design a cloud-only monitor for my property-brief pipeline. Every five minutes, review events since last_seen. Normalize each error into a fingerprint, group repeats in a rolling 15-minute window, and alert only when the same fingerprint appears three times or affects multiple listings. Hold matching updates, prepare one review batch, and require approval before publishing or emailing. Store last_seen, fingerprint, listing ID, source URL, and disposition in a Google Sheet state file.

links.label: xAI · Using Grok Bot to detect and respond to incidents
xAI · X Subscription and Grok Bot access

stories.headline: Oil above $114 puts energy, inflation, and rates back on one dashboard
stories.summary: Brent crude moved above $114 a barrel as Middle East tensions intensified, while global markets shifted toward safer assets ahead of next week’s central-bank meetings. The practical signal is not a one-day market move: energy costs, inflation expectations, borrowing costs, and AI infrastructure spending are now interacting at the same time.
stories.whatChanged: Reuters reported Brent above $114 amid renewed attacks and escalating regional risk. Investors moved toward U.S. Treasuries while the Federal Reserve and several other central banks prepare decisions next week. Markets remain fluid, so treat the price as a dated snapshot.
stories.whyItMatters: For governmental and tribal audits, sustained fuel and borrowing-cost pressure can flow into budgets, grants, estimates, capital plans, liquidity, and subsequent-event discussions.
stories.prompt: Add a one-page macro sensitivity note to this planning file. Trace sustained oil above $110 and higher-for-longer rates to fuel, utilities, travel, construction, debt service, grant budgets, estimates, liquidity, and going concern. Identify the account or assertion affected, the evidence to request, and the threshold that would trigger an updated conclusion. Keep management assumptions separate from auditor analysis.

links.label: Reuters · Global markets: Safety first, October 23
Reuters · Central banks, energy, and AI earnings week ahead

watch.label: Regression-test agents from real failures
watch.note: Save representative inputs, use exact checks where possible, calibrate model graders against human judgments, and rerun prior passing cases after every prompt or model change. OpenAI · Oct 16

watch.label: GPT-6 Pro can split a task across parallel agents
watch.note: The rollout is limited to eligible Pro users and managed-workspace settings. Best use: independent extraction, tie-out, and presentation lanes that reconcile before delivery.

briefings.title: Personalized Weekly Briefing — October 16, 2026
briefings.theme: Build the dashboard. Keep the evidence visible.
briefings.deck: This week’s strongest workflow idea is Claude’s query-visible dashboard beta—an unusually good fit for your SEFA issue review and bank-reconciliation work. The other four stories cover a new reasoning model, an immediate ChatGPT model change, a bundled Grok plan, and a world-economy signal worth carrying into planning.

stories.headline: Claude Dashboards exposes the query behind every chart
stories.summary: Claude can now turn a connected warehouse or app into a dashboard by writing the queries, building charts, and showing each query with its last-refresh time. Anthropic positions the beta for quick exploratory questions—not as a substitute for deeper analysis—so the visible logic is the feature that matters most.
stories.whatChanged: Access: beta on Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise; Enterprise owners must enable it. The dashboard needs a connected data source or app. Each chart exposes what it counted and when the data last refreshed.
stories.whyItMatters: Your current SEFA-issues workbook and January–March bank-reconciliation package are natural candidates for a reviewer-friendly view that keeps the source logic inspectable.
stories.prompt: Build a read-only dashboard from this manager-ready SEFA issues workbook. Include: issue status; program and ALN; potential adjustment; evidence gap; owner; and next action. Show the exact source query and last-refreshed time for every view. Do not alter source data. Flag unmatched rows, duplicate keys, and totals that do not tie.

links.label: Anthropic · Get started with Claude Dashboards
Anthropic · Artifacts availability and plan notes

stories.headline: Gemini 4 Argon reaches the Gemini app for Pro and Ultra
stories.summary: Google moved Gemini 4 Argon from preview into the Gemini app and AI Mode for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers, targeting difficult multi-step work in finance, legal, science, and engineering. Antigravity access remains Ultra-only; public API pricing is introductory through November 30.
stories.whatChanged: Access: Gemini app and AI Mode on Google AI Pro and Ultra; Antigravity on Ultra only. Google lists introductory API pricing of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, rising to $4/$20 after November 30, 2026.
stories.whyItMatters: It gives you a fresh independent-review lane for complex, cross-file work such as reconciling a SEFA draft, issue log, and supporting evidence without changing the source package.
stories.prompt: Act as an independent reviewer of this approved SEFA package. Build a conflict matrix linking each issue to program/ALN, supporting file, amount, exact evidence citation, and proposed next step. Separate observed facts, inferences, and unresolved questions. Do not infer missing amounts or overwrite the manager-ready conclusion.

stories.headline: GPT-5.5 is retired from ChatGPT, Work, and Codex
stories.summary: OpenAI removed GPT-5.5 from ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex on October 14. API access is unaffected, but any saved cloud workflow that depended on the model’s particular formatting or judgment should be re-baselined instead of assumed equivalent.
stories.whatChanged: The retirement applies to the ChatGPT model picker, ChatGPT Work, and Codex. OpenAI says API access is unchanged. The note does not promise that a specific replacement will reproduce prior outputs, so treat migration as a testing event.
stories.whyItMatters: Your repeatable reconciliation, indexing, and manager-email workflows are exactly where silent changes in row counts, exception logic, or citations are most expensive.
stories.prompt: Regression-test this established bank-reconciliation workflow using the same sanitized input and known-good output. Compare row counts, totals, unmatched items, exception classifications, source citations, and final formatting. Report only differences, their likely cause, and the review risk. Do not revise the source files.

stories.headline: xAI bundles Grok Bot and shared usage into one X Subscription
stories.summary: The new X Subscription combines Grok chat, voice, image/video tools, Grok Bot, X, and Cursor under shared model usage. New customers can buy it now; the option to switch is rolling out to existing SuperGrok, Cursor, and X Premium subscribers, who can also keep their current plans.
stories.whatChanged: Plans: Free $0, Plus $8, Premium $30, Super $100, Ultra $200 per month; xAI says regional pricing may vary. Premium includes SuperGrok, Cursor Pro, and X Premium+. Existing subscribers may not see the switch option yet because rollout is staged.
stories.whyItMatters: This is the first practical route to Grok Bot plus broader Grok access in one subscription—but only saves money if you actually use the bundled services.
stories.prompt: Before I switch plans, build a one-page comparison of my current monthly spend and actual usage across SuperGrok, X Premium, and Cursor versus X Subscription Premium. Separate web/iOS features from desktop-only benefits. Flag staged availability, overlapping entitlements, and anything I would lose. Recommend “keep” or “switch” only if the savings and access are verified.

stories.headline: AI investment props up growth while energy and debt raise the floor on risk
stories.summary: The IMF’s October outlook projects 3.1% global growth in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027, with AI investment and trade supporting activity. It simultaneously warns that higher energy and food prices, conflict, debt, and an uneven distribution of gains leave the outlook tilted to the downside.
stories.whatChanged: The IMF says global resilience is increasingly uneven: countries tied to the AI-investment boom are benefiting while energy importers and lower-income economies face greater pressure. Its near-term inflation forecast reaches 4.7% globally, largely from energy and food.
stories.whyItMatters: For planning and review, the combination of higher-for-longer rates, energy volatility, and uneven demand is more useful than the headline growth number alone.
stories.prompt: Add a concise macro-watch section to this planning memo. Map higher energy costs, higher-for-longer rates, and uneven demand to the client’s debt service, liquidity, estimates, impairment, and going-concern assumptions. Define the evidence or threshold that would trigger an update. Keep this separate from management’s assertions.

links.label: IMF · October 2026 World Economic Outlook summary
Reuters · AI investment, war, and debt risks

briefings.title: Personalized Weekly Briefing — October 9, 2026
briefings.theme: The interface is becoming part of the answer.
briefings.deck: The most useful shift this week is not another benchmark: ChatGPT can now choose interactive controls, comparisons, and diagrams when plain text is not enough. Four workflow changes follow, plus one urgent U.S. news snapshot.

stories.headline: GPT-6 can now build the interface that best fits the answer
stories.summary: ChatGPT’s new Intelligent UI can combine prose with diagrams, side-by-side comparisons, calculators, and small interactive tools directly in a response. It can also begin answering while it continues thinking or using tools, adding findings without requiring another prompt.
stories.whatChanged: Paid plans use GPT-6 Sol; Free and Go use GPT-6 Luna. The rollout began globally for Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise on October 7 and for Free/Go on October 8. Enterprise access can depend on admin settings. The Astra-powered Pro reasoning option does not support Intelligent UI, and Work/Codex models did not change with this release.
stories.whyItMatters: Your property due-diligence reports, SFUL indexes, and audit status memos can become inspectable decision tools instead of long static pages—while keeping sources and uncertainty visible.
stories.prompt: Using the attached property due-diligence memorandum, create a mobile-friendly interactive decision surface with: a source-linked issue matrix; price, HOA, commute, and repair assumptions I can change; a red/yellow/green risk view that explains every classification; and a print-ready conclusion. Do not add facts that are not in the memo. Mark unknowns explicitly.

stories.headline: Claude Haiku 5.5 turns repetitive review into a low-cost first pass
stories.summary: Anthropic’s fastest small model is designed for summaries, compaction, classification, database queries, and browser work. Anthropic says it costs about 75% less per task than Haiku 4.5 on average, while Sonnet 5.5 cache reads were cut in half.
stories.whatChanged: Haiku 5.5 is available across Anthropic’s platforms and major clouds. For prompts up to 100,000 tokens, API pricing is $0.10 per million input tokens, $0.50 per million output tokens, and $0.01 per million cache-read tokens. Monthly API credit is rolling out to Max and Team subscribers: $100 for Max 5x, $200 for Max 20x, and up to $500 pooled for Team.
stories.whyItMatters: Your 22-selection Cocopah SFUL support file and kitchen-photo inventory both contain high-volume, low-judgment steps that can be delegated cheaply, reserving the stronger model—and your attention—for conflicting evidence and conclusions.
stories.prompt: Process each indexed selection independently. Extract document type, vendor/payee, date, amount, selection number, supporting-agent section, and missing-evidence flags. Return strict JSON plus a one-row exception summary. Do not conclude whether the item passes; route conflicts, unreadable pages, and missing support to the reviewer.

stories.headline: ChatGPT can now accept audio files as source material
stories.summary: Paid ChatGPT plans and workspaces can upload audio for transcription, summaries, questions, and follow-up drafts. This moves recorded client walkthroughs and interviews into the same source-grounded workflow as PDFs and spreadsheets.
stories.whatChanged: Attach a supported audio file and ask ChatGPT to transcribe or analyze it. Availability can vary by workspace settings, region, client version, and model. OpenAI warns that transcripts may contain errors and language performance varies, so high-stakes facts still need source verification.
stories.whyItMatters: A Sage Intacct export walkthrough, pension explanation, or controls interview can be converted into a timestamped memo and a PBC request list—provided recording consent and your firm’s data policy are satisfied.
stories.prompt: Transcribe this approved recording verbatim enough to preserve accounting terms. Then create: (1) a timestamped process narrative, (2) systems and reports mentioned, (3) control owners and frequencies, (4) unresolved questions, and (5) a draft PBC request list. Quote no more than needed and label uncertain words with timestamps.

stories.headline: Google opens SynthID Detector globally for AI-media provenance checks
stories.summary: Anyone can now upload an image, video, or audio file to check for invisible SynthID watermarks from Google and participating partners, including OpenAI, NVIDIA, and Kakao. The tool is available globally in English and adds a useful verification step—but it is not a universal detector.
stories.whatChanged: Google says SynthID has already watermarked more than 180 billion images and videos plus 240,000 years of audio. Detector access is now global in English. Important limitation: “No watermark found” does not prove media is human-made; the tool only recognizes supported watermarks and participating systems.
stories.whyItMatters: For property due diligence and your photo inventory, the detector gives you one more way to flag virtual staging, altered listing media, or generated imagery before treating a picture as evidence.
stories.prompt: For one shortlisted property, check the most decision-relevant listing images—roof, HVAC, kitchen, windows, and structural areas. Record filename, source URL, upload date, SynthID result, and whether the image appears virtually staged. Treat a negative result as “no supported watermark detected,” not proof of authenticity.

links.label: Google DeepMind · global SynthID Detector access

stories.headline: Category 3 Hurricane Isaias is approaching the Alabama–Florida Gulf Coast
stories.summary: Isaias strengthened to 120 mph and is forecast to make landfall Friday evening near the Alabama–Florida line. Officials warn of life-threatening storm surge, damaging winds, flash flooding, and tornadoes; some coastal areas are under mandatory evacuation orders.
stories.whatChanged: NOAA says Isaias is at or near major-hurricane strength ahead of landfall. The National Weather Service forecasts 5–7 feet of storm-surge inundation along parts of the Panhandle coast, with widespread 4–10 inches of rain and localized totals near 15 inches. Conditions can change quickly; use current official advisories.
stories.whyItMatters: This is a significant U.S. emergency with likely travel, logistics, insurance, and recovery effects across the Gulf Coast and Southeast—even if Arizona is outside the impact area.
stories.prompt: If you have travel, clients, family, or vendors in the affected region, check the current NHC advisory and local emergency-management instructions rather than relying on this morning snapshot. Avoid travel into warning areas and treat evacuation orders as authoritative.

links.label: Associated Press · current impacts and preparations

briefings.title: Personalized Weekly Briefing — October 2, 2026
briefings.theme: Your workflows are becoming continuously updateable.
briefings.deck: This week’s useful shift: cloud agents and Sites can keep work moving between chats—while faster document models and better phone capture shorten the intake-to-review loop.

stories.headline: Published ChatGPT Sites can now be edited in place—and refreshed on a cloud schedule
stories.summary: You can open a published Site in a desktop browser, request changes, review the proposed result, and republish. Sites can also run recurring cloud work through Automations, creating a practical path for keeping your property-viewing briefs current without rebuilding the page each time.
stories.whatChanged: Editing a published Site now starts a new workflow from the live page; changes do not appear until you review and publish. An owner can also add cloud schedules for recurring work. Limit: Sites remains a rolling public beta for eligible ChatGPT workspaces, Plus, and Pro; scheduled work needs its own usable data source.
stories.whyItMatters: Your property-viewing-briefs project can become a lightweight status monitor: check listing price/status/source freshness, surface only exceptions, then let you approve the revised page.
stories.prompt: Every Friday, review the source links used by this property-viewing Site. Create a change queue showing listing status, price changes, stale or inaccessible sources, and the last verified timestamp. Do not publish automatically. Preserve my layout and ask me to approve any content change before publishing.

links.label: OpenAI · Creating and using ChatGPT Sites

stories.headline: ChatGPT Dots introduces an always-on agent for responsibilities that outlive a conversation
stories.summary: A Dot gets its own cloud computer, connected apps, instructions, and an activity log so it can keep advancing an ongoing goal. It can work on schedules or proactively surface changes, with action rules that let you require approval for sensitive steps.
stories.whatChanged: Dots can maintain context and operate a cloud computer between chats, ask for judgment, and use pre-set action rules. Rollout: gradual for adults on Pro (not EEA, Switzerland, or UK) and Business Premium in supported regions; Enterprise is a limited beta and admin-disabled by default. Creation starts on desktop web or the desktop app, not mobile.
stories.whyItMatters: This is the closest current fit for ongoing PBC readiness—watching approved inputs and preparing an exception report—provided you keep workpaper changes and external messages behind explicit approval.
stories.prompt: Monitor PBC and TB/GL/SEFA bridge readiness. Report only changed inputs with file name, timestamp, tie-out status, owner, and blocker. Never modify workpapers, infer unsupported mappings, post entries, or send messages without my explicit approval.

links.label: OpenAI · Getting started with your Dot

stories.headline: Claude Sonnet 5.5 makes routine document and spreadsheet work faster and cheaper
stories.summary: Anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 is more than 30% faster and can cost up to 30% less for most work because it uses fewer tokens. Its sweet spot is well-scoped everyday work—polished documents, spreadsheets, and source-grounded analysis—rather than the hardest open-ended judgment.
stories.whatChanged: Sonnet 5.5 is available across Claude platforms and major cloud providers. App users default to medium effort; lower effort prioritizes speed and cost, while higher effort adds checks. API pricing is listed at $2 per million input tokens, $10 per million output tokens, and $0.20 per million cache-read tokens.
stories.whyItMatters: For your Cocopah FY2025 bridge, this model looks well suited to first-pass mapping checks and exception extraction; keep unusual accounting treatment and final audit conclusions with a human reviewer or a higher-reasoning pass.
stories.prompt: Compare the approved mapped TB 2025/2024, mapped GL, Jan–Mar 2026 subsequent GL, and PBC TB/GL/SEFA bridge. Return only: duplicate or unmapped accounts; TB-to-GL variances; fund/group exceptions; SEFA candidate tie-outs; subsequent-event flags; and source tab/cell references. Do not post entries or infer unsupported mappings.

stories.headline: ChatGPT’s iOS camera now turns a multi-page capture into one PDF
stories.summary: The iOS camera’s new Scan option captures several pages in sequence and automatically combines them into a single PDF. It is a small feature with immediate value for bank statements, signed support, invoices, and field documents that otherwise arrive as scattered photos.
stories.whatChanged: Open the camera button in ChatGPT for iOS and choose Scan; multiple captured pages are combined into one PDF. Availability: OpenAI says the feature is rolling out on iOS, so it may not appear for every account immediately.
stories.whyItMatters: You can consolidate a bank-statement or PBC packet at the point of capture, reducing page-order errors and giving the review workflow one stable attachment instead of a chain of images.
stories.prompt: For the next non-sensitive test packet, scan every page in order, confirm the page count and date range before upload, then ask: “Create a page-indexed table of statement dates, ending balances, missing pages, and unusual gaps. Cite the PDF page for every finding.” Follow your firm’s approved-data policy.

stories.headline: G7 moves to release 100 million barrels as diesel prices stay under pressure
stories.summary: G7 members agreed to coordinate the release of 100 million barrels of diesel and other fuel reserves through the International Energy Agency over four months, with a substantial diesel share front-loaded into the first 20 days. Markets reacted, but the release is a supply cushion—not proof that fuel costs have permanently normalized.
stories.whatChanged: The coordinated reserve action is intended to ease tight fuel markets quickly, especially diesel. AP reported U.S. diesel at $6.37 per gallon on October 2 after a September 22 record of $6.52; oil prices fell on reserve-release discussions, but the outlook remains volatile.
stories.whyItMatters: Fuel volatility touches client-site travel, shipping, and property operating assumptions—so near-term relief should not be treated as a permanent baseline.
stories.prompt: For travel or property comparisons this month, show fuel-sensitive costs separately and include a simple ±10% sensitivity. Refresh actual quotes before a decision rather than using today’s price as a long-term assumption.

watch.note: Panels, sidebars, file editors, and MCP event-triggered automations move connected apps closer to real workflow surfaces. 02

watch.note: Work and Codex access begins with Pro, then expands to Plus, Business, Enterprise, and Edu; Enterprise/Edu owners may need to enable it.

briefings.title: Weekly Briefing Sep 25
briefings.theme: Voice becomes a working interface, not just a conversation.
briefings.deck: This week’s strongest practical change is ChatGPT Voice gaining access to connected apps and Work on web and mobile. The rest of the briefing turns new finance, model-efficiency, search-cost and interest-rate developments into experiments for your audit, property and recurring-monitor workflows.

stories.headline: ChatGPT Voice can now use plugins—and Work can keep going after you stop speaking
stories.summary: Voice can use the plugins and connected apps already available to your account on web, iOS and Android. In Work, it can also create documents, presentations or spreadsheets and use a browser; if a job is unfinished when the call ends, it can continue in text.
stories.whatChanged: Voice is no longer isolated from cloud tools: it can invoke available plugins, show written results in the chat and hand an unfinished Work task into text for completion.
stories.whyItMatters: This lets you narrate a Sage Intacct export checklist beside a client while ChatGPT maintains the evidence log and drafts the handoff document.
stories.prompt: We are exporting an audit PBC package from Sage Intacct. Maintain a live checklist with report name, entity, period, filters, run date, output filename, page/row count, and exceptions. After every spoken update, restate only the open items. Do not mark an item complete unless I explicitly confirm the export and validation.

stories.headline: ChatGPT Finances adds Experian credit-score tracking and monitoring
stories.summary: Eligible users can connect an Experian report and VantageScore 3.0, ask what is affecting the score and receive alerts for changes such as a new inquiry, account or address. The report updates monthly and the Experian connection is separate from bank accounts connected through Plaid.
stories.whatChanged: Finances now combines bank-account context with an optional, separately authorized credit-report view, while preserving separate connections and disconnect controls.
stories.whyItMatters: This can turn your property-purchase goal into a current mortgage-readiness checklist without requiring a live bank-account connection.
stories.prompt: Using only the connected credit report and the assumptions I provide, build a 90-day mortgage-readiness plan. Separate verified report facts from assumptions, rank actions by likely impact and reversibility, flag anything that could temporarily lower the score, and tell me which questions require a lender or certified financial professional.

stories.headline: Claude Opus 5.5 targets the same class of work with lower cost and faster output
stories.summary: Anthropic says Opus 5.5 performs at Fable 5.1’s level on most work while costing about 40% less than Opus 5 on typical workloads. It lists $4 per million input tokens, $20 per million output tokens, $0.20 cache reads and output more than 30% faster than Opus 5.
stories.whatChanged: The flagship tier is being repositioned around efficiency: lower per-token prices, much cheaper cache reads and fewer tokens or calls on Anthropic’s test workloads.
stories.whyItMatters: Long, source-heavy jobs such as bank-statement consolidation or an evidence-indexed property brief are exactly where fewer calls and cheaper cached context could matter.
stories.prompt: Run the same 20-page bank-statement bundle through my current model and Opus 5.5. Produce identical outputs: page-by-page coverage log, transaction table, opening/closing balance roll-forward, exceptions, and source citations. Score only completeness, arithmetic agreement, unsupported inferences, elapsed time, and total usage cost.

stories.headline: Perplexity Fast Search cuts lightweight web checks to $1 per 1,000 calls
stories.summary: Perplexity added search_type: "fast" for lower-latency web retrieval, priced at $1 per 1,000 Search API requests instead of $5 for standard web search. Its Agent API fast preset now uses the same path, with web-search calls dropping from $2.50 to $1 per 1,000 and Perplexity reporting about 800 ms lower latency.
stories.whatChanged: The same result shape can now come from a cheaper fast path, making a two-stage retrieval design practical without rewriting downstream parsers.
stories.whyItMatters: Your listing-status and AI-news monitors can spend pennies on first-pass freshness checks, keep state in Google Sheets, and reserve full research for genuinely changed pages.
stories.prompt: For each tracked URL, read url, last_seen_title, last_seen_date, content_hash, and checked_at from Google Sheets. Use Fast Search first. If title/date/hash is unchanged, update checked_at only and stop. If changed, missing, contradictory, or older than the expected cadence, escalate to standard search and return only the changed fields plus direct evidence links.

stories.headline: The Federal Reserve raises rates to 3.75%–4.00% as inflation stays broad
stories.summary: The FOMC unanimously raised its target range by a quarter point on September 16. This week, several Fed officials said persistent inflation—not only energy or tariff shocks—supported the move, reinforcing the risk that borrowing costs remain elevated.
stories.whatChanged: The direction reversed from the 2025 easing cycle: the Fed tightened by 25 basis points, and this week’s commentary emphasized inflation persistence across the economy.
stories.whyItMatters: For your property search, the immediate practical variable is the actual lender quote and monthly-payment sensitivity, not a guess about the next Fed meeting.
stories.prompt: Build a property-offer sensitivity table using my actual lender quote, not an assumed Fed pass-through. Show monthly principal and interest at the quoted rate, quoted rate ±0.50%, and quoted rate ±1.00%, holding price and down payment constant. Label taxes, insurance, HOA and maintenance separately, and do not present the result as financial advice.

watch.label: GPT-6 Sol and Luna in Work
watch.note: OpenAI added both models on September 22; plan and workspace settings control access and reasoning levels, so benchmark only after they appear in your picker.

watch.label: Grok 4.7 is not yet a SuperGrok story
watch.note: xAI launched it September 21 in Grok Build, Cursor, API and third-party cloud routes; the announcement does not claim consumer Grok or SuperGrok availability.

briefings.title: Weekly Briefing Sep 18
briefings.theme: Your work is moving into the document.
briefings.deck: ChatGPT’s newest step is unusually practical for an auditor: it can now sit beside a Word workpaper, revise selected text and adjust formatting. The rest of this week is about keeping identities, reusable workflows and evidence paths under control.

stories.headline: ChatGPT arrives inside Microsoft Word
stories.summary: ChatGPT’s Microsoft add-in now supports Word alongside Excel and PowerPoint. From the sidebar it can draft from notes, summarize a document, revise selected text, and adjust headings or formatting; the Marketplace listing also says it can bring connected sources into the Word workflow.
stories.whatChanged: The assistant now works against the open document and selected text instead of requiring a paste-export-repaste loop. OpenAI warns that important numbers, citations and claims still require primary-source verification.
stories.whyItMatters: This is well suited to your short experience writeups, status memos and workpaper conclusions: the source draft stays visible while you tighten wording and formatting, but the audit evidence remains outside the model’s authority.
stories.prompt: Review only the selected conclusion paragraph. Preserve every amount, date, person, assertion and cross-reference exactly. Improve clarity and concision for an external-audit workpaper. Then list any statement that appears unsupported or internally inconsistent; do not silently correct it.

stories.headline: Multiple-account plugin connections expand beyond Google’s core apps
stories.summary: ChatGPT now lets you connect multiple accounts to plugins beyond Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Contacts. That means personal and work identities can live in one conversation without signing out and reconnecting each service.
stories.whatChanged: The earlier multi-account support was limited to three Google services; the September 17 update broadens the pattern to plugins generally.
stories.whyItMatters: You actively use separate Gmail identities for formal communications and personal property work. The useful part is less re-authentication; the control risk is asking the right question against the wrong account.
stories.prompt: Before using any connected account, state the service and account identity you intend to search or act through. Keep firm/audit data and personal/property data in separate tasks. If the selected identity is ambiguous, stop before reading or sending anything.

stories.headline: Custom GPT migration is starting—and custom actions will not come along automatically
stories.summary: OpenAI plans to retire custom GPTs and move their reusable instructions into plugin skills. Enterprise migration was targeted for September 17; new custom-GPT creation is planned to end September 25, with retirement scheduled for December 11.
stories.whatChanged: A migrated GPT becomes read-only until retirement. Its replacement plugin starts private, and access must be re-shared and tested; public-GPT access does not guarantee access to the replacement.
stories.whyItMatters: Any reusable audit, property-brief or HTML-generator GPT should be inventoried now. The highest-risk break is a hidden custom action that previously sent data or called a workflow.
stories.prompt: Create a migration inventory with columns: GPT name, creator/workspace, business purpose, users, instructions captured, reference files, custom actions, replacement app/MCP, three regression prompts, expected output, owner, and tested date. Flag every custom action as “rebuild required.”

stories.headline: Perplexity Projects can now store a remote MCP connection once
stories.summary: Perplexity’s Agent API added custom connectors for remote MCP servers. A Project administrator registers the server URL and credential once; later runs reference a connector ID instead of resending the MCP secret every request.
stories.whatChanged: Perplexity stores connection settings and credentials at the Project level. Managed connectors currently include GitHub, Slack, Google Drive, Datadog, Linear and Notion; a custom connector can point at another remote MCP server.
stories.whyItMatters: This fits your preference for cloud-hosted tools and makes a Google-Sheets state service or property-listing MCP reusable across scheduled runs without repeating a large tool definition or embedding the MCP credential in each script.
stories.prompt: Pilot one read-only connector first. Expose only: get_state(run_key), upsert_state(run_key, last_seen_id, checked_at), and list_recent_changes(since). Keep large history in Sheets; return only changed rows plus stable IDs. Measure input tokens before and after deferred tool discovery.

stories.headline: Iran claims a tanker strike as Hormuz traffic remains roughly 90% below prewar levels
stories.summary: Iran said it struck the Togo-flagged tanker Trend over an allegedly unauthorized passage; AP could not independently confirm the claim. A separate tanker was reported hit by an unknown projectile, with its crew safe and fire extinguished, while military-facilitated traffic through the strait remains sharply reduced.
stories.whatChanged: The latest risk is not only a single claimed strike: multiple projectile incidents and authorization warnings are affecting one of the world’s most important oil-shipping chokepoints.
stories.whyItMatters: This is the week’s clearest global transmission channel into everyday costs: constrained energy shipping can lift oil, inflation expectations, borrowing costs and market volatility.

watch.label: Claude’s Life Sciences Verification Program
watch.note: Anthropic launched a September 17 program for vetted life-sciences access—important governance direction, but not a practical audit feature yet.

watch.label: Manual model choice returns
watch.note: ChatGPT Plus and Pro retired automatic Instant-to-Thinking switching on September 14; explicitly choose reasoning for reconciliations and source-heavy reviews.

briefings.title: Friday Briefing Sep 11
briefings.theme: Data moves closer to the work.
briefings.deck: This week’s useful shift is not another model score: connected files, governed business data and source-traceable finance work are converging inside cloud AI. Here is what deserves a test—and what still needs a control.

stories.headline: ChatGPT can now turn connected business data into an interactive report
stories.summary: The new Data plugin in ChatGPT Work and Codex can investigate changes and build interactive dashboards from connected business data. On the same day, Box, Dropbox and SharePoint joined Google Drive in ChatGPT Library, letting web users work across source folders without repeated uploads and follow citations back to the files.
stories.whatChanged: One cloud workflow can now find the PBC folder, query the connected data, explain a variance and produce a reviewable visual deliverable. That reduces upload churn, but inherited permissions are not a substitute for engagement-level scoping.
stories.whyItMatters: For your TB/GL and audit dashboard work, this is the closest productized path yet from authorized source files to a source-linked, interactive deliverable.
stories.prompt: Use @Data with the selected TB/GL folder. Reconcile beginning balance + activity to ending balance; flag accounts over my threshold; build an interactive variance dashboard by account and month; cite every figure to its source file; list unresolved mapping or completeness questions separately. Do not infer missing values.

stories.headline: ChatGPT for Financial Services makes traceability—and firm templates—first-class
stories.summary: OpenAI launched a tailored ChatGPT Work experience with GPT‑6 Astra, built-in premium financial data, granular source tracing and interactive charts. Admins can publish Excel, Word and PowerPoint templates, while compliance teams can export supported workspace logs.
stories.whatChanged: The important design signal is the bundle: licensed data, evidence highlighting, standardized output templates, role-based controls and logs in one governed workspace. OpenAI says 50+ connectors sit in the wider ecosystem.
stories.whyItMatters: Even without eligibility, this is a useful blueprint for an audit AI control stack: authoritative inputs, reproducible calculations, source-level review, locked templates and retained activity evidence.
stories.prompt: Draft a one-page control matrix for an AI-assisted financial analysis workflow. Cover: approved data sources, completeness checks, recalculation, source-level citations, template/version locking, reviewer sign-off, exception handling, access by role, retention, and log export. Separate preventive, detective, and governance controls.

stories.headline: Gemini 3.8 Flash targets long-horizon agent work at Flash pricing
stories.summary: Google says Gemini 3.8 Flash improves on 3.7 across software engineering, agentic tasks and multi-step professional reasoning while keeping the introductory price at $0.75 per million input and $3.75 per million output tokens. Perplexity’s Agent API added the same model in September, including a lower cached-input rate.
stories.whatChanged: A cheaper frontier model can now serve as the repeatable QA pass after a stronger model builds the artifact—especially where the task is a long checklist rather than a single answer.
stories.whyItMatters: For your portable HTML and property-site work, this creates a plausible low-cost second-review layer for mobile layout, keyboard access, state persistence and data-label consistency.
stories.prompt: Review this web artifact as an independent QA agent. Test at 390px and desktop widths; keyboard-only navigation; light/dark contrast; reduced motion; empty/error states; persistent favorites; chart labels vs source data; and every outbound link. Return only: blocking defects, reproducible steps, expected result, and the smallest safe fix.

stories.headline: Perplexity’s remote MCP now signs into claude.ai with OAuth
stories.summary: Perplexity’s hosted MCP endpoint now supports OAuth, so compatible cloud clients such as claude.ai can connect through a Perplexity sign-in instead of a pasted API key. You choose the API organization to bill during sign-in; API keys remain available for clients without OAuth.
stories.whatChanged: The remote endpoint is . OAuth removes the secret-copying step and makes organization selection explicit during connection.
stories.whyItMatters: This fits your cloud-only integration preference and gives a clean research connector for recurring runs without storing a long-lived key in every workflow.
stories.prompt: In claude.ai, add https://api.perplexity.ai/mcp as a custom remote connector, sign in with Perplexity, and select the intended billing organization. First test: find primary-source updates from the last 7 days, return title/date/direct URL, and omit any claim that cannot be tied to a source.

stories.headline: Congo’s fast-growing Ebola outbreak reaches a seventh province
stories.summary: The outbreak has reached Sud-Ubangi in western Democratic Republic of Congo, the first confirmed westward spread, with a rare Bundibugyo strain detected there. AP reports 6,942 cases and 3,349 deaths; conflict, displacement, staff shortages and limited strain-matched vaccine options are complicating containment.
stories.whatChanged: The geographic jump matters more than the headline count: spread from the conflict-hit east to the west increases cross-border risk toward Central African Republic and potentially South Sudan.
stories.whyItMatters: This is the one world development this week worth keeping on your situational-awareness list, especially for travel, supply-chain or multinational client exposure.
stories.tryThis: For decisions, bookmark the official situation reports and record the report date beside every figure; do not reuse today’s case count as a standing fact.

briefings.title: Friday Briefing Sep 4
briefings.theme: The week AI work became more capable—and more governed.
briefings.deck: Astra is the headline, but the practical story is broader: better workspace controls, voice-first Gmail, and a remarkably cheap cloud research tier.

stories.headline: GPT-6 Astra aims at finished work, not just stronger answers
stories.summary: OpenAI says Astra improves coding, research, computer use, and complex multi-step work, including producing documents, spreadsheets, and presentations that follow supplied templates. Access began with a limited set of organizations on September 3; Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and API availability is planned over the coming days, so it may not yet appear in your model picker.
stories.whatChanged: Astra is framed as an end-to-end work model: it can adapt when requirements change and carry a task from research through a formatted deliverable. The useful caveat is availability—this is a staged release, not universal access today.
stories.whyItMatters: Your strongest test is a complete audit loop, such as reconciling a TB to support and returning a review-ready workbook in your established format.
stories.tryThis: Using the attached TB, GL, and prior-year workpaper, build the requested audit schedule in the supplied template. Preserve formulas, identify every exception, independently recompute totals, and finish with a Purpose / Scope / Procedures / Conclusion memo. Do not conclude until all source-to-output ties are documented.
stories.prompt: Using the attached TB, GL, and prior-year workpaper, build the requested audit schedule in the supplied template. Preserve formulas, identify every exception, independently recompute totals, and finish with a Purpose / Scope / Procedures / Conclusion memo. Do not conclude until all source-to-output ties are documented.

stories.headline: ChatGPT Work adds governed plugins and fresher workspace memory
stories.summary: OpenAI added beta Zendesk and OneNote plugins for eligible workspaces, along with centralized plugin permissions. Enterprise and Edu are also receiving improved memory that can keep relevant context current across chats; Enterprise begins with roughly two weeks of admin-controlled early access before default enablement for eligible workspaces.
stories.whatChanged: Admins can search, install, enable, or restrict plugins by role from one settings surface, while users connect their own authorized accounts. Improved memory includes a reviewable summary, and admins or users can revert to legacy saved memories.
stories.whyItMatters: This is the governance layer your Kayenta and other audit projects need before cross-chat memory or Office content becomes dependable workpaper context.
stories.tryThis: If your work workspace receives improved memory, review its memory summary before the next Kayenta status run. Remove stale engagement facts, then compare the run’s conclusions with the authoritative tracker and source files—memory should guide retrieval, never replace evidence.
stories.prompt: Review the workspace memory summary for this engagement. Identify stale, unsupported, or conflicting facts, then compare each retained fact against the authoritative tracker and source files. Treat memory as retrieval guidance only, never as audit evidence.

stories.headline: Gmail Live turns inbox search into a voice conversation
stories.summary: Google is rolling out Gmail Live globally in English on iOS and Android, letting you ask follow-up questions about inbox details and see the supporting emails in the transcript. Gmail Live requires Google AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra; Docs Live is iOS/Android for Pro and Ultra, while business Workspace support is still “coming soon.”
stories.whatChanged: The features were previewed in May and began general mobile rollout on September 3. Gmail Live retrieves and cites inbox information; Docs Live can structure spoken ideas and, with permission, pull context from Gmail, Drive, Chat, and the web.
stories.whyItMatters: On your iPhone, this could become the fastest way to extract a viewing time or lender detail from Kathy’s thread while keeping the original email one tap away.
stories.tryThis: Open Gmail on iPhone and ask: “From Kathy’s latest property-viewing thread, list only confirmed addresses, viewing times, access instructions, and unresolved financing restrictions. Cite the email for every item.” Verify each cited message before using it.
stories.prompt: From Kathy’s latest property-viewing thread, list only confirmed addresses, viewing times, access instructions, and unresolved financing restrictions. Cite the email for every item. Do not infer missing details.

stories.headline: A $0.15-per-million-token research sidecar is now realistic
stories.summary: Perplexity’s Agent and Router APIs added GLM 5.3 Flash at $0.15 per million uncached input tokens, $0.03 cached input, and $0.50 output. It is not a free tier, but the published rates make it practical to use for cheap preprocessing—classifying listings, compacting state, or normalizing OCR text—before sending only the difficult exceptions to a frontier model.
stories.whatChanged: The new router model joins automatic prompt-cache keys for presets, which Perplexity says can reduce recurring preset costs by about 5% depending on cache reuse. Availability is through the cloud-hosted API and requires a Perplexity API account.
stories.whyItMatters: Your property and audit automations carry large repeated instructions; a cheap normalization pass plus a tiny exception packet can reduce both token use and context clutter.
stories.tryThis: Have the low-cost model convert each new listing into one fixed JSON schema and compare it with your Google Sheet state. Send the frontier model only changed fields, conflicts, and missing high-risk facts; retain the original source URL and agent value (chatgpt or KDT) unchanged.
stories.prompt: Normalize each new listing into the fixed schema, compare it with the current Google Sheet row by listing_key and agent, and output only: changed fields, conflicts, and missing high-risk facts. Preserve source URL and agent exactly; never convert KDT rows to chatgpt.

stories.headline: Global food prices reach their highest level since late 2022
stories.summary: The UN FAO Food Price Index rose 1.9% in August to 133.3, with every major commodity group higher; it was 2.5% above a year earlier but still 16.8% below the March 2022 peak. Sugar jumped 11.9%, while cereal prices rose amid weather concerns, disrupted Black Sea logistics, and input pressure linked to the Strait of Hormuz.
stories.whatChanged: The September 4 release shows price pressure broadening across cereals, oils, meat, dairy, and sugar rather than staying isolated. FAO also highlighted lower crop prospects in parts of Europe and the United States.
stories.whyItMatters: This is an early signal for household grocery costs and for audit clients whose budgets or operations are sensitive to food, fuel, or transportation inputs.
stories.tryThis: For any food-service or assistance-program client, compare year-to-date food and transport costs with budget and prior year before planning analytics. Treat the FAO index as external context—not direct audit evidence for a recorded balance.
stories.prompt: Compare year-to-date food and transportation expense with budget and prior year. Investigate whether price, volume, or program mix explains the variance, and use the FAO index only as external context—not as direct audit evidence.

briefings.title: Daily Briefing Sep 2
briefings.deck: Today’s useful thread is not a bigger benchmark number. It is lower-cost repeated context, multi-account access, and cleaner evidence bridges: the plumbing that makes cloud workflows sustainable.

stories.headline: Claude Fable 5.1 makes long, repeated agent work materially cheaper
stories.summary: Anthropic released Fable 5.1 across Claude.ai, Cowork, its API, AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure. It says typical token-billed workloads cost about 25% less than Fable 5, with savings up to roughly 45% for context-heavy agentic work, mainly because cache reads fell 75% to $0.25 per million tokens.
stories.whyItMatters: Your long scheduled prompts repeatedly contain the same property-search rules, audit safeguards, schemas, and state contracts. Fable 5.1’s economics reward converting that stable block into cacheable context while keeping only the run-specific delta dynamic.
stories.tryThis: Cache-friendly prompt split Keep the stable instructions byte-identical; put timestamps and state after them.
stories.prompt: Restructure this automation into two blocks. Block A is immutable: role, safeguards, output schema, field definitions, and source hierarchy. Block B is run-specific: date, last successful issue, new feedback, and changed records. Keep Block A byte-for-byte stable between runs so prompt caching can reuse it.

stories.summary: ChatGPT now supports multiple connected Gmail, Google Calendar, and Google Contacts accounts on supported Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise plans across web and iOS. You can search personal and formal inboxes together or compare calendars without forwarding mail between accounts.
stories.whyItMatters: This directly addresses your sqeaky4100/ktevis1990 split for ChatGPT research: connect both, name the target account in the request, and keep Gmail’s own forwarding/send-as setup as a separate human-email convenience.
stories.tryThis: Two-inbox test Run read-only first and verify every result shows which inbox received it.
stories.prompt: Search both connected Gmail accounts for messages from the last 30 days about Apple Card, property listings, or rental tours. Label every result with the receiving account. Do not mark, move, delete, draft, or send anything.

stories.summary: Agent API presets now reuse stable system prompts and tool definitions automatically, which Perplexity estimates can cut frequent-preset costs by about 5% depending on cache use. The same cloud endpoint also added Gemini 3.7 Flash and Grok 4.6, while its remote MCP server requires no local installation.
stories.whyItMatters: One inexpensive hosted research layer can handle fresh web evidence and citations while your main ChatGPT or Claude agent focuses on judgment, file work, and final presentation.
stories.tryThis: Cheap research sidecar Measure tokens before and after; savings come from smaller evidence handoffs, not model switching alone.
stories.prompt: Use Perplexity's remote MCP only for discovery and citation gathering. Return a compact JSON array with title, source URL, publication date, exact supporting excerpt, and confidence. Pass that small evidence package to the main agent; do not pass full scraped pages unless requested.

stories.headline: Build a pension disclosure bridge—don’t force one TB account to answer two questions
stories.summary: Employee contributions and employer pension expense are different measures, so a single payroll deduction or pension account may align with only one disclosure. A reusable Excel bridge should separately map employee-withholding accounts, employer pension expense, cash/remittance activity, and year-end accruals, then explain the reconciling difference.
stories.whyItMatters: This turns the recurring “which of two amounts aligns with prior-year wording?” issue into auditable logic with an account-level trail rather than a judgment buried in chat.
stories.tryThis: Formula pattern Start from the GL/TB and use the draft financial statements only as a comparison—not the source.
stories.prompt: Create a Pension Bridge sheet with columns: TB Account, Description, Employee/Employer classification, Current-year activity, Cash paid, Accrual change, Disclosure bucket, and Source. Use XLOOKUP for the account map, FILTER to display each bucket, SUMIFS for totals, and LET to calculate Employee Contributions, Employer Pension Expense, and the reconciliation once with readable variable names. Flag unmapped accounts and any bridge difference above the audit threshold.

stories.headline: U.S.–Iran fighting surges; Hormuz and oil return to the center of global risk
stories.summary: The United States struck Iranian military sites along the southern coast, and Iran responded with missiles and drones aimed at U.S. assets and allies in Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait, and Iraq—the largest exchange since July. Initial U.S. assessments reported no American casualties, while claims surrounding a strike on an Iranian wedding remain disputed; Brent rose to around $95 as shipping risk intensified.
stories.whyItMatters: The Strait of Hormuz carried roughly one-fifth of traded oil before the conflict, so sustained disruption can flow quickly into fuel costs, inflation expectations, travel, markets, and client budgets.
stories.watchFor: Watch verified shipping volumes, official casualty assessments, and whether attacks spread to additional Gulf infrastructure. Treat state-media casualty and attribution claims as provisional until independently confirmed.

briefings.title: Daily Briefing Sep 1
briefings.theme: Agents move from chat to real work
briefings.deck: Today’s clearest signal: cloud agents are gaining persistent context, authenticated browsing, event triggers, and task-specific integrations—the pieces needed to automate work without a local machine.

stories.headline: ChatGPT Work gains event triggers and signed-in cloud browsing
stories.summary: Work can now trigger from new Gmail messages, Slack messages, or GitHub pull-request activity, and its browser on web and mobile can continue tasks on supported signed-in sites. Webhook tasks are available to Plus and Pro; authenticated browsing is also Plus/Pro and still pauses for consequential approvals.
stories.whyItMatters: This is the closest cloud-only replacement yet for workflows that previously needed a continuously running local browser: a client email can initiate research, document preparation, or a status update while your laptop is off.
stories.tryThis: PBC-email triage pilot Trigger on one trusted client sender first; keep tracker writes and replies approval-gated.
stories.prompt: When a new Gmail message arrives from a named audit client contact, read it and its attachments read-only. Match each requested item to the existing PBC tracker, summarize what changed, identify duplicates or conflicts, and draft proposed tracker updates. Do not write to the tracker or send email until I approve.

stories.headline: Grok Bot reaches SuperGrok plans—and plugs into X
stories.summary: Grok Bot is now included with SuperGrok, SuperGrok Plus, and SuperGrok Heavy, with usage separate from the main Grok allowance. Paid users can connect X, receive starter API credits, and ask a cloud Bot to search posts, review timelines, check mentions, and surface trends.
stories.whyItMatters: The separate Bot allowance makes it practical to offload a recurring research lane—such as frontier-AI release monitoring—without consuming the interactive Grok quota you use for ad hoc questions.
stories.tryThis: Frontier release scout Use X for discovery, then verify every claim against an official release note before acting.
stories.prompt: Each morning, scan official X accounts for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, xAI, and Perplexity. Return only product availability changes for cloud, web, or iOS users. Separate released, rolling out, preview, and rumor. Include the original post link and plan restrictions.

stories.headline: Claude memory now follows work into cloud Cowork
stories.summary: Claude’s editable memory topics now work across ordinary chat and Cowork in the cloud. Memory is on by default for Free, Pro, and Max, but off by default for Team and Enterprise; sensitive topics remain excluded unless explicitly enabled.
stories.whyItMatters: Your preferences and working conventions can follow a Cowork run without a giant bootstrap prompt, but exact run counters, authoritative listing history, and audit status still belong in structured files—not probabilistic memory.
stories.tryThis: Split semantic and exact state Let memory save tokens; let Sheets preserve auditability and counters.
stories.prompt: Use memory only for stable preferences, style, and workflow conventions. At the start of every run, read the Google Sheet control row for last successful issue, exact listing keys, and current open-item status. At the end, write only verified deltas and re-read the written range.

stories.headline: Ask Gemini turns Google Chat into a Workspace command center
stories.summary: Ask Gemini can search Gmail, Drive, and Calendar; summarize conversations; create content; and manage meetings or tasks from a persistent session in Google Chat. The rollout is gradual for eligible Workspace editions, with temporary higher limits through October 1.
stories.whyItMatters: It could provide a fast “what changed across mail and Drive?” layer for audit status checks, but your personal Google One subscription alone likely does not qualify.
stories.tryThis: Check eligibility first If your work Workspace is eligible, test a read-only engagement recap before enabling task or calendar actions.
stories.prompt: Search my Gmail, Drive, and Calendar for changes related to [engagement] since [date]. Return: new client evidence, scheduling changes, unresolved conflicts, and source links. Read only; do not send messages, alter files, or create events.

stories.headline: Nepal flood toll passes 1,000 as rescuers reach remote valleys
stories.summary: Reuters reports more than 1,050 confirmed deaths and roughly 4,000 people missing after an August 26 glacier collapse sent floodwater and debris through Himalayan valleys. More than 11,000 people have been rescued, while damaged roads, power systems, and hydropower tunnels continue to slow access.
stories.whyItMatters: The scale makes this one of the world’s defining humanitarian and climate-risk stories this week, with consequences for Nepal’s communities, tourism, and hydroelectric infrastructure.
stories.watchFor: Casualty figures remain provisional. Watch official rescue updates and established news organizations; avoid sharing unverified victim lists or dramatic social clips without location and date confirmation.
